abstract: We show a practical application of the Google Gemini large-language-model for simulating tandem mass spectra for compounds from the Blood Exposome Database. This approach bypasses the need for domain-specific model training, suggesting that the chemical fragmentation knowledge could be latently encoded within the Gemini model. General-purpose LLMs represent a useful and accessible tool for expanding in-silico spectral libraries and may accelerate the compound annotation in mass spectrometry-based metabolomics and exposomics.
